hints.text: Both quantities equal mean divided by daily standard deviation, multiplied by sqrt(252), under these assumptions.

solution.setup: Annualize the daily mean-to-volatility ratio by sqrt(252).
solution.reasoning: The ratio is (1/15)·sqrt(252)≈1.06. With one year of independent observations, the mean's t-statistic is the same value. A t-stat near 1 is not strong evidence against a zero true mean.
solution.finalAnswer: Annualized Sharpe≈1.06; t-stat≈1.06; evidence is weak.
solution.sanityCheck: A seemingly respectable Sharpe can still be statistically noisy when observed for only one year.

keyInsight: Sharpe magnitude and estimation uncertainty must be considered together.
recognitionCues: A short return history asks for both performance and statistical confidence.
commonMistakes: Calling a Sharpe above 1 conclusive without considering sample length.
followUps: Approximately how many independent years would raise the t-stat to 2 if Sharpe stayed constant?

source.notes: Original variant of a publicly reported interview family associated with Citadel Securities, Two Sigma, Jump Trading.

title: Is One Year of Sharpe Convincing?
problem: A strategy has 252 independent daily returns with sample mean 0.08% and sample standard deviation 1.2%. Estimate its annualized Sharpe ratio and the t-statistic for a zero mean. Is this strong evidence of skill?
